question.problem:
Find the vector in the subspace spanned by $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ 
that is closest to the vector $x,$ where 

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are linearly independent. 

The closest vector to $x$ in the subspace spanned by $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace, which is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{30}[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
